problem:
Consider the following initial value problem:

$$
{y}^{′}={y}^{2}-{x}^{2},\,y(1)=2
$$

Using the implicit Euler method with step size $Δx=0.5,$ the new value ${y}_{\text{new}}$ is obtained by solving the equation $g({y}_{\text{new}})=0$ at each step.
Which of the following is the **specific function** $g({y}_{\text{new}})$ used in the first step?

feedback.problem:
Consider the following initial value problem:

$$
{y}^{′}=x\,{y}^{2}-y,\,y(1)=1
$$

Using the implicit Euler method with step size $Δx=0.5,$ the new value ${y}_{\text{new}}$ is obtained by solving the equation $g({y}_{\text{new}})=0$ at each step.
Which of the following is the **specific function** $g({y}_{\text{new}})$ used in the first step?
feedback.worked_solution:
For an initial value problem

$$
{y}^{′}=f(x,y),\,{y}_{0}=y({x}_{0}),
$$

the implicit Euler method with step size $Δx$ is given by

$$
Δy={y}_{\text{new}}^{′}\cdot Δx,
$$

with ${y}_{\text{new}}^{′}=f({x}_{\text{new}},{y}_{\text{new}})$ evaluated at the next $x$ and $y$ values.

In general, $Δy$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}Δy & ={y}_{\text{new}}^{′}\cdot Δx \\  & =({x}_{\text{new}}({y}_{\text{new}})^{2}-{y}_{\text{new}})\cdot 0.5 \\  & =0.5{x}_{\text{new}}({y}_{\text{new}})^{2}-0.5{y}_{\text{new}}.\end{aligned}
$$

We substitute this into ${y}_{\text{new}}=y+Δy$ and move all terms to the left-hand side and define the resulting expression as $g({y}_{\text{new}}):$

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}_{\text{new}} & =y+Δy \\ {y}_{\text{new}} & =y+0.5{x}_{\text{new}}({y}_{\text{new}})^{2}-0.5{y}_{\text{new}} \\ {{1.5{y}_{\text{new}}-0.5{x}_{\text{new}}({y}_{\text{new}})^{2}-y}_{⏟}}_{g({y}_{\text{new}})} & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the general form of the function $g$ for step size $Δx=0.5$ is

$$
g({y}_{\text{new}})=1.5{y}_{\text{new}}-0.5{x}_{\text{new}}({y}_{\text{new}})^{2}-y.
$$

Now, in the first step, the new $x$ value is ${x}_{\text{new}}=x+Δx=1+0.5=1.5.$ Therefore, the function used in the first step is

$$
\begin{aligned}g({y}_{\text{new}}) & =1.5{y}_{\text{new}}-0.5\cdot 1.5\,({y}_{\text{new}})^{2}-1 \\  & =1.5{y}_{\text{new}}-0.75({y}_{\text{new}})^{2}-1.\end{aligned}
$$
